init_modem_driver_request.source_behavior: The AP IPA driver uses service 0x31/version1 as both a local server (instance 1) and a client of modem instance 2. Its client builds 0x0021 from live IPA_MEM_PART values, SRAM geometry, SMEM restriction and endpoint mappings, then validates the modem response. The response can carry modem_driver_init_pending; when true, the AP must wait for the separate 0x0035 completion request. The AP server also handles 0x0020 indication registration and may send 0x0022 after its own QMI initialization completes. None of these states prove WLAN readiness, and the request is not safely reproducible as an all-zero or guessed static packet.
init_modem_driver_request.offline_status: rust/src/qcom_ipa.rs implements the bounded no_std INIT_MODEM_DRIVER codec, source maximum, optional-field rules, and range validation. rust/src/sunfish_ipa_profile.rs derives the Sunfish IPA v4.2 request from static rules plus required live SRAM, endpoint, and uC-state inputs; rust/src/sunfish_ipa_snapshot.rs parses matched Lineage hw_type/gen_reg output without inventing unknown endpoint or uC state. The client is integrated in the host GLINK/QMI model, but the phone runtime does not enable it. rust/src/qcom_ipa_service.rs provides the bounded AP-side 0x0020/0x0035 response core and gated 0x0022 indication. The GLINK/QMI session, FIFO adapter, and native owner now expose AP service registration, readiness-controlled availability, source-matched response queuing, and indication queuing. AP response state commits only after both GLINK RX_DONE and QRTR RESUME_TX; response and indication completion tokens have offline exchange coverage. The opt-in IpaServerServices runtime adapter now prepares the instance-1 endpoint, gates advertisement on a generation-matched ApReadyPermit and QRTR peer HELLO, dispatches only the exact modem peer requests, and commits responses/indications after both GLINK RX_DONE and QRTR RESUME_TX. Native owner request demultiplexing leaves IPA and SERVREG requests for their dedicated dispatchers instead of passing them to storage/heap handlers. No trusted live IPA hardware-readiness provider exists and the default phone path remains NoServices, so this adapter is compiled/tested offline but is not enabled on the phone. The saved successful Lineage trace lacks raw QMI response fields, so it does not reveal whether modem_driver_init_pending was set. The no-radio AArch64 synthetic-codec probe was temporarily booted on 2026-10-24. The first response-fixture correction still omitted a byte; the exact check was factored into shared code, host-tested, and now passes. The latest rebuilt image awaits target retest. The read-only Lineage capture can inspect IPA hw_type/gen_reg and existing init log records without root or state changes. The read-only LineageOS IPA capture was rerun on 2026-10-23 with the Pixel attached; ordinary shell still could not read hw_type or gen_reg. The kernel log recorded the INIT_MODEM_DRIVER request and response 39 ms apart without a raw payload. Boot logs showed modem out of reset, QRTR readiness, wlan_pd state 0x1fffffff acknowledged, icnss QMI connected at 0x980, and WLAN FW ready 0xd87 followed by the WMA ready event. APPS_WAN_CONS and IPA uC-loaded state remain unknown; no evidence yet proves this exchange causes the custom modem failure. The native IpaModemInitServices adapter now reserves the client before QRTR startup, sends one source-matched request after exact modem IPA service discovery, and gates MSA progression on a successful response. If modem_driver_init_pending is true, it also requires the AP IPA server to commit the separate 0x0035 completion response. This adapter is only exercised with a test-only InitPermit: no trusted live IPA provider can mint the production permit, so the phone runtime does not enable it.

common_transport_gaps: The fatal-trace build delegates to the measured-wait discovery path. It performs QRTR HELLO and passive service inventory, not remote-storage or memory service registration.
Discovery service() only accepts a 52-byte QRTR v1 NEW_SERVER control datagram; it cannot dispatch QMI DATA packets to local service endpoints.
The discovery buffers are 64 bytes and verified/copy52 assumes 52 payload bytes. A minimum heap allocation datagram is 32-byte QRTR + 7-byte QMI + four 7-byte TLVs = 67 bytes.
Storage IOVEC request arrays and other messages require bounded variable-length receiving and GLINK fragment handling, not only larger constants.
No native block mapping or separate modem-accessible storage/heap pool appears in the fatal-trace system. Its private buffers do not supply those remote address contracts.
Optional standalone SERVREG replies are not implementations of service 0x0e or 0x34 and are not enabled by the fatal-trace build.

qrtr_control.mode: Native owner enables the controller before any receive intent; codec-only simulation remains explicit.
qrtr_control.profile: Exact QRTR-v1 52-byte controls; fixed peer identity; local/broadcast control destination; no forwarding or remote lookup registration.
qrtr_control.local_readiness: Trusted backend availability separate from decoder registration. Generic handlers validate backend state and bind to the owner before readiness; the native runtime has no real action backend attached and stays unannounced.
qrtr_control.announcements: One HELLO; NEW_SERVER/DEL_SERVER use service descriptors and configured local endpoint ports. Announcements require peer HELLO, local HELLO publication and explicit readiness.
qrtr_control.publication: Shares eight bounded TX slots; commit readiness/announcement state only after whole known publication; await GLINK completion without QRTR credit. Existing QMI replies retain both completion requirements.
qrtr_control.remote_registry: 64 entries keyed by peer port; duplicate coalescing, descriptor replacement, exact stale-delete protection, no eviction or authority grants.
qrtr_control.wlfw_discovery: Read-only passive lookup of one exact peer announcement: service 0x45, packed version/instance 1. Wrong versions and ambiguous duplicates fail closed; native reads repeat the live SMEM lifecycle gate. QRTR NEW_LOOKUP is local to the name service and is never forwarded over GLINK.
qrtr_control.receives: Target two backed receive intents within eight RX slots; consumed controls retire after RX_DONE publication; fresh monotonic one-shot IDs.
qrtr_control.peer_loss: BYE/DEL_PROC quarantine; client/server closure affecting pending QMI state stops without releasing buffers or native RX tail; no automatic generation/restart.
qrtr_control.native_test: Real native buffers, SMEM gate, FIFO and IRQ owner decode peer HELLO plus completion; unready backends remain unannounced.

service_handlers.profile: Generation/node/endpoint bindings; four allowlisted partition enums and truthful geometry/write/durability metadata; page-aligned, guarded, disjoint pools and bounded exclusions. Configuration checks are not proof of native ownership.
service_handlers.storage_handles: Eight full-peer-scoped handles; monotonic IDs never recycle. One confirmed shared storage lease serves same-peer open handles and is reclaimed only after the last closes.
service_handlers.storage_io: Validate all IOVECs before effects. Check disk/granted-range/total bounds and reject overlapping spans or zero-length entries. One private 4096-byte chunk per IO step; all writes sync before success. Known partial failures are not atomic and latch device error.
service_handlers.heap_policy: Client1/processor0; one contiguous active lease; page alignment satisfies supported enum0..11. Return exact requested length after zeroing/confirmed ownership. Exact active retries are idempotent; conflicting requests and stale successful sequences fail.
service_handlers.heap_free: Exact owner/address/length, one block. Confirm reclaim before retirement. Never reuse freed physical pages within the generation because FREE has no sequence field; later grants advance a bounded reservation cursor.
service_handlers.backend: Owned opaque backend plus non-dropping receipts. Observation identity covers all pools and partition bindings. Grant serial/region/peer/generation/mode and current ownership must match. Uncertainty, lost lifecycle or unwinding IO stops and retains state without retry or cleanup.
service_handlers.owner_integration: Bind one exact handler instance and endpoint profile. activate_handlers enables readiness only after validation. notified_with_handlers runs bounded transport plus one action step. Ordinary notification/reply calls reject bypass. Cache completed results through FlowBusy/NoCapacity without repeated effects.
service_handlers.native_status: Generic storage/SCM-pool composition is implemented and tested with verified disposable host files. No native UFS/block provider or truthful boot/SCM ownership gate is attached; native service announcements remain disabled.
service_handlers.proof_limit: Host private images and simulated committed/durability/ownership states; AArch64 generic codegen uses an action-failing stand-in. This does not prove persistence, SCM, cache behavior or device operation.

pools_scm.faults: Pre-submit known staging failure leaves prior lease valid. Set target owner Unknown before submission. Kernel/transport error, nonzero x0, completion or post-call lifecycle failure stops without a success receipt. Failed reclaim retains receipt/reservation. Lifecycle observation loss invalidates both owners. Unwind latches before external calls. No Drop actions.
pools_scm.data: Every granted page needs successful full-page zero/readback. At most4096 data bytes per call. Active receipt bounds every shared storage copy; all host heap data APIs denied after assignment. Monotonic manager instance and grant serial stop stale receipts.

storage_backend.profile: Four ordered enum/capability bindings, generation, device fingerprint, source/checkpoint digests, unique object IDs, fixed capacity/write/durability metadata. Profile parsing is not source/device authentication.
storage_backend.io: Sector512 aligned, checked offset+length, at most4096 bytes per data action. One provider call per operation; no hidden short IO retries. Short reads fail; short/ambiguous writes latch dirty and stop. Failed sync never clears dirty or acknowledges persistence.
storage_backend.composition_lifetime: One exact storage/pool pair with independent observed identities and a unique combined identity. Both lifetimes checked around every action. Initial storage must be clean and pools host-owned. Storage loss after successful grant withholds receipt/address; pool loss after disk write withholds success. Resources retained without automatic rollback.
storage_backend.host_setup: Open only existing regular files without create/truncate/append. Reject symlinks, hardlinks, aliases, incomplete metadata, lock conflicts and checkpoint mismatch; compare inode, device, length, mode and setup timestamps. Private locked descriptors, bounded full-image SHA256 before attachment.
storage_backend.host_persistence: One positional read/write per data action and explicit File.sync_all. Successful write plus sync was verified across reopening and fresh writer/reader processes; other files remained unchanged.
storage_backend.host_dependencies: Separate host crate/lockfile pins cached sha2 0.10.9; no new main Rust/Microkit dependency. Runner uses locked offline Cargo with warnings denied and a temporary target directory.
storage_backend.source_authority: Device, origin and expected current checkpoint authenticity are caller-supplied trusted inputs. Checkpoint must be explicitly updated for verified mutable-file restart. No rollback protection or phone data provisioner is implemented.
storage_backend.host_lock_limit: Advisory locks require cooperating exclusive users, not protection from arbitrary external writers. File descriptors close on explicit object/process teardown; closure is not a flush acknowledgement. Faults retain owned descriptors.
storage_backend.native_status: No native instance or service readiness is enabled; the native target has no UFS/block provider. Two host tests exercise owner activation and request/reply routing with fake files/pools; the host file adapter runs only on disposable fixtures.
proof_limits: Host filesystem persistence and process reopening are not a physical power-cut, host-crash or Pixel UFS durability test.
SCM outcomes remain simulated in these tests. Native boot/ownership contract is still required.
No actual modem partition image was read, copied, created or collected. No phone, ADB, Fastboot, partition or live SCM action occurred.

observation.interpretation: The value has SMMU client processing enabled (CLIENTPD=0), global fault reporting and interrupt enabled (GFRE=1, GFIE=1), unidentified-stream faults enabled (USFCFG=1), and multiple-stream-match conflicts configured to fault (SMCFCFG=1). MTCFG=0 leaves the MemAttr field inactive. The source label SCR0 does not establish that the secure bank was read; the register bank depends on the probe's security state. The observed UFS context bank is not translating, and the five checked WLAN SIDs have no matching route in the displayed stream-match table. This does not authorize DMA; the exact WLAN SID match mask, ownership transfer, and context-bank delegation remain unverified.

native_storage_resource_audit.interpretation: The command codec, caller-selected offline LUN discovery flow, primary GPT partition validator, HCI core, bounded IRQ dispatcher, and capability-gated volatile adapters are testable components, not a physical block provider. The separate candidate Microkit map proves only static MMIO/IRQ layout and includes no DMA authority or live platform bring-up. Native attachment still requires a production authority owner for UFS/PHY/ICE, clocks, rails, reset, interconnect, DMA/SMMU, and IRQ, followed by physical LUN and both-table partition verification against trusted device identity. The host regular-file adapter supplies neither. The new qcom_ufs_modem_storage adapter composes a verified paired-GPT proof with the modem remote-storage trait and enforces bounded extents and live SID 0x300 route-to-context-bank gates, but it has no production BlockIo or physical-media path. The qcom_ufs_scsi_block_io bridge submits bounded READ(10), WRITE(10), and SYNCHRONIZE CACHE commands through the existing Host core, but has only synthetic RegisterIo/DmaIo/ObservationSource fixtures and is not a production storage path.

current_owner_note: Historical phone traces remain unchanged. Offline GLINK/QMI handlers compose with validated pools and a host file backend; the host provider proves filesystem sync/reopen only. The default native owner keeps services disabled; opt-in attach_with_handlers retains caller-owned storage/heap handlers, and opt-in IpaServerServices wires the AP IPA QMI server behind a provider-minted readiness permit. No trusted production storage, IPA, SCM-ownership, UFS or DMA provider is constructed or attached. A separate TftpServerServices adapter can route QRTR requests over an explicitly supplied fixed-extent random-access source, reading only requested DATA blocks and retiring a transfer on source I/O or extent faults; ReadSourceCell adapts mutable storage I/O with live extent checks. Authorized-image constructors remain test-only and the Pixel runtime selects only the payload-free observer. No WLAN firmware bytes have been served and no production image source or applicable license authorization is selected. UFS codec/HCI, capability-gated native adapters, the resource lifecycle model, exact-SID UFS route-to-aperture composition and ordered SMMU install planning, a bounded one-snapshot IRQ dispatcher, the verified-GPT-to-modem-storage adapter, and the READ(10)/WRITE(10)/SYNCHRONIZE CACHE bridge pass synthetic tests. The UFS provider is also composed with the SCM pool backend in a host integration test. The bridge has no production RegisterIo/DmaIo or live ObservationSource. The planner rejects the inherited broad SID 0x300 route; the candidate Microkit profile maps UFS MMIO/IRQ but has no DMA aperture, and the dispatcher is not connected to an operational host. A production Gate/PlatformIo, actual DMA/SMMU authority, UFS platform bring-up, SCM ownership, physical GPT verification, and physical UFS provider remain absent, so service readiness stays false.
